title: The interface-type check (exit 13) reads the doctor's own subscription type from the ROS graph, not the publisher's type
trigger: A publisher on a configured topic uses a different message type than the config expects, and that type sorts alphabetically after the expected one. Examples: sensor_msgs/msg/Imu (or any std_msgs type) on /chassis/odom, or std_msgs/msg/Float64 on /clock. This also affects every report where a topic has no publisher at all.
expected: Per the doctor_checks precedence: 13 env_or_interface_error with 'odom: message type X != expected nav_msgs/msg/Odometry'. For a topic without a publisher, msg_type should be empty (None).
actual: observe() creates its subscriptions before discovery, so get_topic_names_and_types() also lists the doctor's own subscription type. types[k] = graph[name][0] then picks the first entry of a sorted set (rmw_dds_common keeps a std::set per topic). A wrong-type publisher that sorts after the expected type is hidden. Its data never matches the subscription, so the doctor gives 12 'degraded: publisher present but no message' for odom, or 10 'simulation paused or stopped' for /clock, instead of 13. The runner then retries the 12 case three times. The JSON msg_type field records the doctor's own type even when there is no publisher.
evidence: Recorded artifacts show the doctor's own type is in the graph: artifacts/d1/real-03-closed/doctor-20260930-000733.json (Isaac closed, no publishers) and artifacts/d5/demo/doctor/doctor-20260930-021108.json both report odom (present=False, msg_type='nav_msgs/msg/Odometry'), and the same for tf and lidar. Fixed-input repro: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash -lc "cd /mnt/d/RoboSim-Eval && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 .../review-wf/doctor_config/repro_1_types.py" gave: 'odom: publisher type sensor_msgs/msg/Imu graph list [nav_msgs/msg/Odometry, sensor_msgs/msg/Imu] -> doctor sees nav_msgs/msg/Odometry; verdict degraded exit 12'; 'clock: publisher type std_msgs/msg/Float64 -> doctor sees rosgraph_msgs/msg/Clock; verdict sim_not_advancing exit 10'; geometry_msgs/msg/PoseStamped (sorts first) -> exit 13. The sorted-set order comes from the upstream rmw_dds_common source and was not checked live, because creating nodes was not allowed. With any order, the listed type is not reliably the publisher's. The unit test (test_wrong_message_type_is_an_interface_error) injects msg_type directly, and test_doctor_fake.sh has no wrong-type case.
fix_direction: Take publisher types from node.get_publishers_info_by_topic(name) (TopicEndpointInfo.topic_type). Flag 13 if any publisher type differs, and set msg_type None when there is no publisher. Add a fake-node case that publishes a wrong type whose name sorts after the expected type.

verification.repro: S=/mnt/c/Users/Administrator/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/d--RoboSim-Eval/59900d3e-5384-418b-8374-e6a8773582da/scratchpad/review-wf/verify-doctor_config; MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash -lc "cd /mnt/d/RoboSim-Eval && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 $S/v1_types.py". The script runs the real doctor.observe() and evaluate() against a fake in-process rclpy that uses virtual time and creates no DDS entities. Its graph lists, per topic, the sorted set of endpoint types, the doctor's own subscriptions included, as rmw_dds_common does. Output: 'odom publisher sensor_msgs/msg/Imu -> odom.msg_type=nav_msgs/msg/Odometry present=True | degraded exit 12 | publisher present but no message'; the same for std_msgs/msg/String; 'odom publisher geometry_msgs/msg/PoseStamped -> env_or_interface_error exit 13'; 'clock publisher std_msgs/msg/Float64 -> clock_type=rosgraph_msgs/msg/Clock | sim_not_advancing exit 10 | ...(simulation paused or stopped)'; 'no publishers at all -> odom.msg_type=nav_msgs/msg/Odometry present=False'. The last line matches the recorded artifacts exactly: artifacts/d1/real-03-closed/doctor-20260930-000733.json and artifacts/d5/demo/doctor/doctor-20260930-021108.json both have odom/tf/lidar present=False with msg_type set to the expected type.
verification.reasoning: The code at HEAD matches the report. observe() creates its subscriptions at doctor.py:89-96, before the discovery loop. Line 106 then takes types[k] = graph[name][0]. The recorded 'Isaac closed' reports prove that the doctor's own subscription type is in the graph: msg_type is filled in even though present=False. So msg_type does not come from the publisher. The check at doctor_checks.py:180-185 fires only when the first listed type differs from the expected one. count_publishers counts every writer on the topic, whatever its type, and DDS will not match a reader to a writer of another type. A wrong-type publisher that is hidden behind the doctor's own type therefore gives present=True with no samples: 12 for a stream, or 10 with 'simulation paused or stopped' for /clock. Only a type that sorts first gives 13. I could not check the exact list order live because node creation is not allowed. If the doctor's own entry came first by insertion order, the check would miss every mismatch. The unit test injects msg_type directly, and test_doctor_fake.sh has no wrong-type case. Downgraded from Major to Minor: the doctor still exits non-zero and the runner still refuses the run, so no false pass results. What is wrong is the category (13 vs 12/10), the operator message and the JSON msg_type field. The trigger is a misconfigured publisher, not the normal path.
verification.fix_direction: Take publisher types from node.get_publishers_info_by_topic(name) (TopicEndpointInfo.topic_type), excluding the doctor itself. Report 13 when any publisher type differs, and set msg_type None when there is no publisher. Add a fake-node case that publishes a wrong type which sorts after the expected type (e.g. sensor_msgs/msg/Imu on /chassis/odom).

title: _positive accepts NaN, inf, numeric strings and booleans, and NaN thresholds silently turn off doctor, evaluator and deadline checks
trigger: Any threshold written as .nan, 'nan', .inf, '1e999' or true. Examples: doctor clock_stall_s: .nan, odom {min_rate_hz: .nan, max_age_s: .nan}, run.position_tolerance_m: .nan, dropout_wall_s: 'nan', timeouts.nav_wall_s: .nan.
expected: Load error: every limit should be a finite number greater than 0.
actual: Every comparison with NaN is False. The doctor reports healthy with /clock 3.04 s stale and odom 4.04 s stale. The evaluator reports 'reached/complete/pass' for Nav2 SUCCEEDED with ground truth 7 m from the goal and 30 s gaps in every required stream, which is the false-success case A5 forbids. deadline_exceeded never fires, so waits are unbounded. inf has the same effect on the limits and on window_s/discovery_timeout_s (doctor.sh then hits its 60 s cap). A NaN sim.reset_check turns the reset verification off.
evidence: repro_3_nan.py output: '_positive(.nan) -> nan', "_positive('nan') -> nan", '_positive(.inf) -> inf', '_positive(true) -> 1.0'; 'doctor with NaN thresholds: clock last age 3.04 odom last age 4.04 -> healthy 0'; 'evaluator with NaN tolerance/dropout: 7 m off, 30 s gaps -> reached complete pass'; 'nav_wall_s NaN: deadline after 1e6 s wall -> None'. tests/test_config.py tests only window_s: 0.
fix_direction: In _positive, reject bool and str inputs and require math.isfinite(number) and number > 0. Add tests for nan, inf, strings and booleans.

verification.repro: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash -lc "cd /mnt/d/RoboSim-Eval && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 $S/v2_config.py" prints: '_positive(nan) -> nan', "_positive('nan') -> nan", '_positive(inf) -> inf', "_positive('1e999') -> inf", '_positive(True) -> 1.0'; 'doctor NaN thresholds, frozen clock (0 s progress, last 3.04 s ago), odom last 5.00 s ago -> healthy 0'; 'evaluator NaN tol/dropout, gt 7 m off, 30 s gaps -> reached/pass/complete/pass'; 'EXECUTING deadline after 1e6 s wall / 1e6 s sim with NaN limits -> None'. The last case uses a config loaded with 'position_tolerance_m: .nan'.
verification.reasoning: config.py:106-113 only rejects `number <= 0`, and that is False for NaN. It never rejects inf, bool or numeric strings. Every downstream comparison (doctor_checks.py:146/148/200/204, evaluator.py:116/138, runner_fsm.deadline_exceeded, sim_math.check_reset:60-64) uses '>' or '<' against the threshold, so NaN turns each check off. The result is a false 'healthy' from the doctor, a false 'reached/pass' that A5 explicitly forbids, and unbounded waits. tests/test_config.py tests only window_s: 0. Minor: a real .nan/inf in the config is unlikely and needs deliberate YAML such as '.nan', but the validator exists exactly to catch this and does not.
verification.fix_direction: In _positive, reject bool and str inputs and require math.isfinite(number) and number > 0. Add tests for .nan, .inf, 'nan' and true.

title: Config typos and collisions load silently: unknown keys, duplicate YAML keys, unknown obstacle assets, duplicate obstacle names and an empty required-stream list
trigger: Any of: 'obstacle:' instead of 'obstacles:' in bypass; 'asset: lowbox' in collision; 'expected_outcome: unreachable'; 'contact: {ignore_prefix: …}'; a second 'normal:' key under scenarios; run.streams.required: []; two obstacles named box_1.
expected: Load errors for unknown keys, duplicate mapping keys, asset names not in sim.obstacle_assets, duplicate obstacle names and an empty required list, as is already done for inject and timeouts keys.
actual: Each case loads without warning. bypass runs with no obstacle and can pass as 'reached'. runner.py:265 obstacle_assets.get(ob.asset, obstacle_usd) replaces the unknown asset with the 1 m lidar-visible box, so the collision fault is never injected. expect_outcome silently becomes 'reached'. Ground-plane contacts become collisions. PyYAML keeps the last duplicate scenario, so 'normal' gets another goal. required: [] means data is never judged incomplete. Duplicate obstacle names fail only after the reset, when SpawnEntity is called with allow_renaming=False.
evidence: repro_4_keys.py output: "1 bypass with 'obstacle:' typo -> () reached"; '2 collision asset lowbox -> uri used by runner: D:/RoboSim-Eval/configs/assets/box_1m.usda'; "3 unreachable with 'expected_outcome' typo -> reached"; "4 contact 'ignore_prefix' typo -> ()"; "5 duplicate 'normal' -> normal goal now Pose2D(x=5.0, y=5.0, yaw=0.0)"; '6 run.streams.required -> ()'; "8 duplicate obstacle names -> ['box_1', 'box_1']".
fix_direction: Validate each section against an allowed key set. Load with a SafeLoader subclass that rejects duplicate keys. Check ob.asset against sim.obstacle_assets and drop the silent fallback in runner.py. Reject duplicate obstacle names and an empty run.streams.required.

verification.repro: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash -lc "cd /mnt/d/RoboSim-Eval && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 $S/v2_config.py" prints: "bypass 'obstacle:' -> () reached/pass/complete/pass"; 'collision asset lowbox -> runner uri D:/RoboSim-Eval/configs/assets/box_1m.usda'; "unreachable 'expected_outcome' -> reached"; "contact 'ignore_prefix' -> ()"; "duplicate 'normal' key -> normal goal Pose2D(x=5.0, y=5.0, yaw=0.0)"; 'required: [] -> () reached/pass/complete/pass'; "duplicate obstacle names -> ['box_1', 'box_1']". Each variant is a one-line edit of the baseline written to scratch.
verification.reasoning: _load_scenarios/_load_run/_load_sim read keys with .get() and defaults. Only the inject and timeouts keys are checked against allowed sets. yaml.safe_load keeps the last of any duplicate keys. runner.py:265 `obstacle_assets.get(ob.asset, simcfg.obstacle_usd)` silently swaps in the 1 m lidar-visible box for an unknown asset, so the collision fault injection is not performed. Together with finding 10, that scenario then validates 'pass'. With required: [] data_status can never be incomplete. Duplicate obstacle names fail only at /spawn_entity (sim_adapter.py:103 allow_renaming=False), after the reset. Each case needs a config typo, so Minor, but several produce a plausible-looking pass instead of a load error.
verification.fix_direction: Validate each section against an allowed key set. Load with a SafeLoader subclass that rejects duplicate mapping keys. Check ob.asset against sim.obstacle_assets at load and remove the silent fallback at runner.py:265. Reject duplicate obstacle names and an empty run.streams.required.

title: --window is not validated, and min_sim_progress_s does not scale with it, so a healthy simulation can be reported as paused
trigger: doctor.sh --window 0, -5, nan or any value up to about 0.6. min_sim_progress_s 0.2 is fixed, and the measured RTF is 0.32 with Nav2 running. --window 100 hits the 60 s cap instead.
expected: Usage error (exit 2) for a non-positive or non-finite window. The progress threshold should scale with the window, or a lower bound on the window should be enforced. Config window_s is already checked to be > 0.
actual: argparse accepts all of these values. window 0 gives 'sim_not_advancing exit 10: no /clock message in 0.0 s (simulation paused or stopped)'. Windows of 0.3, 0.5 and 0.6 s give exit 10 because 'advanced only 0.168 s … (< 0.2 s)'. --window 100 ends as exit 124, reported as 'the doctor hung'.
evidence: repro_2_window.py output: 'argparse accepts --window 0 -> 0.0', '-5 -> -5.0', 'nan -> nan'; 'healthy sim, window 0.0 s -> sim_not_advancing exit 10'; 'window 0.6 s -> sim_not_advancing exit 10 [clock: simulation time advanced only 0.168 s in 0.6 s (< 0.2 s)]'; 'window 1.0 s -> healthy exit 0'.
fix_direction: Validate args.window with the same finite and > 0 rule as the config, bounded by the doctor.sh cap. Either reject windows below something like min_sim_progress_s / 0.25 RTF plus the stall time, or scale min_sim_progress_s with the window.

verification.repro: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash -lc "cd /mnt/d/RoboSim-Eval && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 $S/v3_window.py" calls the real doctor.main(['--config', baseline, '--window', W]) against a fake healthy sim (virtual time, /clock 21 Hz, RTF 0.32). Output: '--window 0 -> exit 10 | sim_not_advancing', '--window -5 -> exit 10', '--window nan -> exit 10', '--window 0.3 -> exit 10 [clock: simulation time advanced only 0.122 s in 0.3 s (< 0.2 s)]', '--window 0.6 -> exit 0', '--window 1.0 -> exit 0'. In this fake the cut-off lies between 0.3 and 0.6 s; the other reviewer saw 0.6 s fail. The exact edge depends on the /clock rate and RTF.
verification.reasoning: argparse type=float (doctor.py:149) accepts 0, negative and nan values, and line 158 uses them unchecked. The config path validates window_s > 0, but the CLI override bypasses that. At doctor.py:109 a window <= 0 or NaN skips observation, so a running sim is reported as paused (exit 10). min_sim_progress_s is a fixed 0.2 sim s (doctor_checks.py:200), so at the measured RTF of about 0.32 any window below about 0.6 s fails on a healthy sim. By code, a window above about 50 s ends at doctor.sh's `timeout 60`, exit 124, 'the doctor hung'. The runner never passes --window, so only manual use is affected: Minor.
verification.fix_direction: Validate --window with the same finite, > 0 rule as the config, and cap it below the doctor.sh limit minus discovery and start-up time. Either enforce a minimum window such as (min_sim_progress_s / minimum expected RTF) + clock_stall_s, or scale min_sim_progress_s with the window.

title: Malformed configs and env errors that stop ROS from starting exit with 1 and a traceback, not the documented 2 (config) or 13 (environment)
trigger: A YAML syntax error in the config; a null value such as 'goal: {…, yaw: }'; a stream entry with no values ('lidar:'); a non-mapping 'topics'. Also, in a direct 'python3 -m robosim_eval.doctor' run, an RMW_IMPLEMENTATION or ROS_DOMAIN_ID that makes rclpy.init or Node() raise RCLError.
expected: doctor.py docstring and doctor.sh: 2 = usage/config error, 13 = environment error with the highest precedence. The runner documents 2 for a config error.
actual: load_config raises yaml.YAMLError, TypeError or AttributeError. main() catches only (OSError, ValueError), so both the doctor and the runner print a traceback and exit 1, a code the runner does not document; a batch then records exit 1 for every attempt. _env_reasons runs only after a successful observe(), so an env problem that breaks rclpy start-up gives exit 1 instead of 13.
evidence: repro_6_exitcodes.py output: 'yaml_syntax robosim_eval.doctor exit 1', 'yaml_syntax robosim_eval.runner exit 1', "null_goal_yaw … exit 1 TypeError: float() argument must be … 'NoneType'", "stream_without_values … exit 1 AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'". The RCLError path was found by reading the code only and was not run, because creating rclpy contexts or nodes was not allowed.
fix_direction: Wrap yaml.YAMLError, TypeError and AttributeError in load_config as ValueError with the key path. Evaluate _env_reasons before observe() and return 13 without touching ROS on a mismatch. Catch RuntimeError from rclpy init in main and map it to 13.

verification.repro: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash -lc "cd /mnt/d/RoboSim-Eval && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 $S/v4_exit.py" runs python3 -m robosim_eval.doctor and python3 -m robosim_eval.runner --scenario normal on four bad configs; load fails before any ROS use and no run dir is created. Output: 'yaml_syntax doctor exit 1 / runner exit 1'; "null_goal_yaw ... exit 1 | TypeError: float() argument must be a string or a real number, not 'NoneType'" (both); "stream_no_values ... exit 1 | AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'" (both). Control case: 'window_s: abc' -> exit 2 'config error' (both).
verification.reasoning: load_config raises yaml.YAMLError, TypeError or AttributeError for these inputs. doctor.py:155 and runner.py:578 catch only (OSError, ValueError), so the process exits 1 with a traceback. The runner does not document exit code 1 (its docstring lists 0/10/11/20/30/31/2), and the doctor calls 1 an 'internal error'. I did not run the RCLError case (rclpy.init/Node failing under a bad RMW_IMPLEMENTATION or ROS_DOMAIN_ID), because it would create an rclpy context. By code it is uncaught (doctor.py:167-171 catches only ImportError/ValueError), and _env_reasons runs only after observe(). doctor.sh forces good RMW and domain values through ros_env.sh, so that sub-path is reachable only by running the module directly. Minor.
verification.fix_direction: In load_config, convert yaml.YAMLError, TypeError and AttributeError into ValueError that names the key path. In doctor.main, evaluate _env_reasons before observe() and return 13 without touching ROS on a mismatch, and map RuntimeError/RCLError from rclpy start-up to 13.

title: The 'type would change' guard treats int and float as the same kind, but ROS 2 parameters are statically typed
trigger: scenarios.<s>.nav2_params: {controller_server.ros__parameters.FollowPath.max_vel_x: 1} (int for a double), or {…FollowPath.vx_samples: 12.5} (float for an integer).
expected: apply_changes should refuse, because its docstring says it raises 'when … the value type would change'. rclcpp static typing rejects an integer override for a parameter declared with a double default (and the reverse) with InvalidParameterTypeException.
actual: The change is accepted. The line becomes 'max_vel_x: 1' or 'vx_samples: 12.5'. The parse-back check passes because 1 == 1.0 in Python. Nav2's controller_server would then fail to configure, and the run would end as a WAIT_READY/start_nav2 error rather than a config error.
evidence: repro_5_nav2.py against the real vendor carter_navigation_params.yaml (read-only): "A …max_vel_x -> [('      max_vel_x: 0.8', '      max_vel_x: 1')] [{… 'old': 0.8, 'new': 1}]"; "A …vx_samples -> [('      vx_samples: 20', '      vx_samples: 12.5')]". The Nav2/rclcpp rejection comes from known rclcpp behaviour; Nav2 was not started (not allowed).
fix_direction: Require type(old) is type(new) for int and float. At minimum, coerce an int to float when the old value is a float and dump it as '1.0'. Add tests for both directions.

verification.repro: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash -lc "cd /mnt/d/RoboSim-Eval && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 $S/v5_nav2.py" reads the real vendor carter_navigation_params.yaml (read-only) and prints: "max_vel_x 1 -> [('      max_vel_x: 0.8', '      max_vel_x: 1')] [{... 'old': 0.8, 'new': 1}]" and "vx_samples 12.5 -> [('      vx_samples: 20', '      vx_samples: 12.5')] [{... 'old': 20, 'new': 12.5}]". Neither is refused.
verification.reasoning: _same_kind (nav2_params.py:33-34) treats int and float as the same kind, and the parse-back check at line 84 passes because 1 == 1.0 in Python. The apply_changes docstring promises to refuse 'the value type would change'. Nav2 DWB declares max_vel_x with a double default and vx_samples with an int default, without dynamic_typing. rclcpp therefore rejects an override of the other type with InvalidParameterTypeException ('Wrong parameter type ... is of type {double}, setting it to {integer} is not allowed'). This is well-known rclcpp behaviour; I did not run it because Nav2 may not be started. controller_server would then fail to configure, and the run would end as a WAIT_READY timeout or start_nav2 error rather than a config error. The runner's in_effect check (runner.py:313) would not help either, since 1.0 == 1. Minor: it needs a declared value written without a decimal point, or the reverse.
verification.fix_direction: Require type(old) is type(new) for int and float, or coerce int to float when the old value is a float and dump it as '1.0'. Add tests for both directions.

title: The dotted-path scheme cannot address real vendor parameters, and the errors are misleading or come late
trigger: nav2_params: {controller_server.ros__parameters.FollowPath.PathAlign.scale: 16.0}. The vendor file has the literal key 'PathAlign.scale', and the same for GoalAlign.scale, PathDist.scale and others. Another trigger is a costmap parameter such as local_costmap.local_costmap.ros__parameters.inflation_layer.inflation_radius.
expected: Either support these keys or reject them at config load with an accurate message. D5 promises that a scenario can declare a Nav2 parameter change.
actual: _lookup splits on every '.', so the critic scale parameters give "not found in the params file" although they exist (value 32.0). Costmap paths pass apply_changes, then write_params writes run_dir/nav2_params.yaml before node_and_param raises 'expected <node>.ros__parameters.<name>'. config.py only checks that the key contains a dot.
evidence: repro_5_nav2.py: "B controller_server.ros__parameters.FollowPath.PathAlign.scale -> ValueError … not found in the params file" and "B   but the vendor file has it: 32.0". repro_7_costmap.py: "apply_changes ok: [{… 'old': 0.8, 'new': 0.9}]" then "ValueError … expected <node>.ros__parameters.<name>".
fix_direction: Take the path as a list of YAML keys, or split on '.ros__parameters.' and use the remainder as the literal parameter name. Support namespaced nodes such as /local_costmap/local_costmap, or reject paths at config load with node_and_param before writing any file.

verification.repro: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash -lc "cd /mnt/d/RoboSim-Eval && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 $S/v5_nav2.py" prints: "vendor literal key 'PathAlign.scale' = 32.0"; "PathAlign.scale -> nav2 parameter 'controller_server.ros__parameters.FollowPath.PathAlign.scale' not found in the params file"; "costmap apply_changes ok: [{'path': 'local_costmap.local_costmap.ros__parameters.inflation_layer.inflation_radius', 'old': 0.8, 'new': 0.9}]"; "write_params: ... expected <node>.ros__parameters.<name> | file left behind: True" (written to a scratch run dir).
verification.reasoning: _lookup (nav2_params.py:23) and the line matcher join or split on every '.'. The vendor keys at lines 216-223 (BaseObstacle.scale, PathAlign.scale, GoalAlign.scale, ...) are literal dotted names, so they cannot be addressed, and the error wrongly says 'not found'. Namespaced nodes (local_costmap.local_costmap...) pass apply_changes. node_and_param then rejects them only after write_params has written nav2_params.yaml. The runner still catches this ValueError in PREPARE (runner.py:193) before Nav2 starts, so 'late' only means after config load, and the only effect is a leftover file. config.py:203 checks only that the key contains a dot. The declared max_vel_x change works, so D5 as demonstrated is fine. This limits which other parameters can be changed and gives a misleading message: Minor.
verification.fix_direction: Split the path on '.ros__parameters.' and treat the remainder as the literal parameter name (or take a list of YAML keys). Support or explicitly reject namespaced nodes with node_and_param at config load, before any file is written.

title: Tests do not pin the documented verdict precedence or the nav2_params safety guards; YAML errors escape the runner handler and leave no manifest
trigger: Mutations run in a scratch copy: (a) env check moved after the clock checks; (b) stream-missing moved before clock-not-advancing; (c) env check moved after stream-missing; (d) parse-back check removed; (e) 'exactly one line' check weakened to 'at least one'. Separately, a vendor or target line that does not re-parse after the edit (anchor on the leaf, a flow mapping across lines, multiple documents).
expected: Each documented rule (13 > 11 > 10 > 11 > 12; 'checked by parsing both texts'; 'exactly one line') is caught by at least one test. apply_changes raises ValueError, as its docstring says, so that runner._prepare records params_error after writing manifest.json.
actual: All five mutations survive. For example, with an env error and a missing stream the verdict could become 11 and no test would notice. apply_changes lets yaml.composer.ComposerError and other YAMLErrors through. runner._prepare catches only (OSError, ValueError), so the exception skips write_manifest and write_resolved_config, and that run directory lacks manifest.json and config.resolved.yaml (A6). The vendor file pinned today has no anchors, so this part is latent.
evidence: mutate2.py: 'env check moved after clock checks SURVIVED 15 passed', 'stream-missing moved before clock-not-advancing SURVIVED 15 passed', 'env check moved after stream-missing SURVIVED 15 passed'. mutate.py: 'no_parse_back_check rc=0 SURVIVED 9 passed', 'no_exactly_one_line_check rc=0 SURVIVED 9 passed'. repro_5_nav2.py D: 'anchored leaf -> yaml.composer ComposerError | is ValueError: False'. artifacts/d1/mutation-check.txt M1-M7 contain no precedence mutation.
fix_direction: Add fixed-input tests that combine two faults (env error + no clock; env error + missing stream; paused clock + missing stream) and assert the documented winner. Add nav2 tests with a duplicate leaf, a flow mapping and a mis-edit that only the parse-back check catches. Convert yaml.YAMLError to ValueError in apply_changes, or write the manifest before deriving params.

verification.repro: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash -lc "PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 $S/v6_mutate.py" copies robosim_eval/ and three test files to $S/mut, applies one mutation at a time and runs test_doctor_checks.py plus test_nav2_params.py from the copy. It confirms the copy is the one imported. Output: 'env after all clock checks -> SURVIVED (24 passed)', 'stream-missing before clock-not-advancing -> SURVIVED', 'env after stream-missing -> SURVIVED', 'stream-missing before clock-missing -> SURVIVED', 'nav2 parse-back check removed -> SURVIVED', 'nav2 exactly-one -> at-least-one -> SURVIVED'. $S/v5_nav2.py: 'anchored leaf -> yaml.composer ComposerError | ValueError? False'.
verification.reasoning: No test combines two faults: env error with a paused or missing clock, or a paused clock with a missing stream. So the documented precedence 13 > 11 > 10 > 11 > 12 is not pinned. test_doctor_fake.sh (healthy/paused/closed/lidar_missing/lidar_slow/rmw_unset) has no combined case either, and artifacts/d1/mutation-check.txt M1-M7 has no precedence mutation. title: Fault-injection scenarios cannot declare their real expectation, so validation_status is inverted for them
trigger: The collision scenario (expect text 'safety must be fail, never pass') and the dropout scenario ('must not be a normal pass: data incomplete') can only declare expect_outcome: reached. Trigger case: the low box is not hit, the pause is too short, or detection regresses.

actual: When the injection has no effect, both scenarios get validation 'pass'. When it works they get 'fail' or 'inconclusive'. The D3 ledger reads these manually ('正确地不判通过'), but a report or batch would show a green pass if collision or dropout detection broke.

title: An unknown obstacle asset name silently spawns the default 1 m box
trigger: A scenario obstacle whose 'asset' is not a key of sim.obstacle_assets, for example a typo 'low-box' in the collision scenario.
expected: Config loading rejects the unknown asset, or the runner fails. The declared fault injection (a low box below the /scan band) must not be replaced by a different obstacle without anyone noticing.
actual: config._load_scenarios never checks asset names. runner uses `simcfg.obstacle_assets.get(ob.asset, simcfg.obstacle_usd)` and spawns box_1m.usda, which the lidar can see. The obstacle_spawned event logs only the declared (wrong) asset name; the substituted uri appears only in facts. The collision scenario's injected fault would silently not be applied.
evidence: repro_asset.py loads a scratch copy of baseline.yaml with collision asset 'low-box' through load_config (no error) and applies the runner.py:265 expression. Output: `declared asset='low-box' -> spawned uri=D:/RoboSim-Eval/configs/assets/box_1m.usda`.
fix_direction: Validate every obstacle asset against sim.obstacle_assets when the config is loaded (config error, exit 2), drop the fallback, and log the uri in the obstacle_spawned event.

verification.repro: verify-simctl/baseline_typo.yaml is a sed copy of configs/baseline.yaml with only `asset: low_box` changed to `asset: low-box` (diff shows line 114 only). repro6_asset.py loads it through load_config and applies runner.py:265's expression. Command: `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash -lc "cd /mnt/d/RoboSim-Eval && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 .../verify-simctl/repro6_asset.py .../verify-simctl/baseline_typo.yaml"`. Output: `scenario=collision obstacle=low_box declared asset='low-box' -> uri=D:/RoboSim-Eval/configs/assets/box_1m.usda` (no config error).
verification.reasoning: config.py stores ob.get('asset','box_1m') without checking it against sim.obstacle_assets. runner.py:265 falls back to obstacle_usd (the 1 m box, which the lidar sees). A typo therefore silently replaces the declared fault injection (a low box below the /scan band) with a visible obstacle. The substitution is not fully hidden: facts.obstacles in result.json records the uri, but the obstacle_spawned event and the scenario label keep the declared name. A likely outcome is a scenario-expectation failure attributed to the system rather than to the config. Minor.
verification.fix_direction: Validate every obstacle asset key against sim.obstacle_assets in load_config (config error, exit 2), remove the silent fallback, and include the uri in the obstacle_spawned event.

title: Run from another checkout, the fake-node tests exercise /mnt/d/RoboSim-Eval's doctor, not the checkout under test
trigger: test_runner_fake.sh or test_doctor_fake.sh is run from a git worktree. Commit 67a8ffa changed test_runner_fake's REPO to 'the checkout this script is in', and docs/plan.md:42 records moving development into a worktree during batches.
expected: Every component a fake test exercises comes from the checkout being tested.
actual: The runner is imported from the worktree, but its doctor step calls the worktree's doctor.sh, which does `cd /mnt/d/RoboSim-Eval` and `python3 -m robosim_eval.doctor`, so the main checkout's doctor runs. test_doctor_fake.sh hard-codes REPO=/mnt/d/RoboSim-Eval and does the same. A doctor change under test is never exercised, and a PASS can come from different code.
evidence: Static: test_runner_fake.sh:13 (REPO from BASH_SOURCE) versus doctor.sh:13/21-22 and test_doctor_fake.sh:12/23 (hard-coded REPO, cd, python3 -m). `git show 67a8ffa -- scripts/wsl/test_runner_fake.sh` shows the REPO change.
fix_direction: Derive REPO from BASH_SOURCE in doctor.sh and test_doctor_fake.sh (and the other wrappers), or make the tests assert the module path they imported.

The runner's WSL constant (runner.py:37-38) is derived from its own file, and the runner calls that doctor.sh on every fake case: PREPARE runs it even with --no-sim (runner.py:206-210). doctor.sh:13/21-22 hard-codes REPO=/mnt/d/RoboSim-Eval, cds there and runs `python3 -m robosim_eval.doctor`, which resolves to the main checkout's module. test_doctor_fake.sh:12 hard-codes the same path.
